answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to hold a unique, randomly assigned data shard and answer frequent, identity-bound retrieval challenges. Like a vertex in a storage network, each agent must prove it actually stores its shard; a copied shard fails when two identities are challenged at different offsets. An attacker on the ledge of cheap duplication must pay real disk and bandwidth per fake identity, unlike an ivory-tower design trusting self-declared identities. Cost then grows linearly per Sybil, making large farms uneconomical.
